title: An exogenous parchment hole separates layout interruption from semantic record reset
summary: A raw source-specific hypothesis treats a physical parchment hole as an external intervention. If writing continues the same record around the hole, a layout-obstacle model survives; if the writer restarts a bounded record with a distinct reset construction, the hole may be an independently observable trigger for a content boundary.

design.mechanism: exogenous-hole interruption with record-continuity versus content-reset alternatives
design.unit: the three text lines interrupted by the admitted f99v parchment hole and one comparable intact local record
design.contrast: physical layout obstacle preserving record scope versus hole-triggered semantic record reset
design.prediction: A continuity model predicts the same active record constraints resume after the hole, with no new reset construction; a reset model predicts a reproducible restart signature or changed record-level participant/field relation immediately after the hole.
design.countermodel: The hole may simply remove writing while the scribe resumes an ordinary line, and any apparent restart may be ordinary paragraph/layout behavior. Neither physical interruption nor proximity alone supplies semantic evidence.
design.falsifier: The post-hole text resumes the same independently established record relation without a restart marker, or an equivalent restart occurs at intact non-hole boundaries; either result removes the hole-specific semantic claim.
design.principal_risk: The exact around-hole writing and any reset construction have not been extracted in this task. Root's native observation of a prominent hole is motivation only. GDT881 separately found no shared text/anatomy stroke construction and does not establish a hole-bound meaning.
design.source_motivation: GDT881 records ordinary short lines, no clear dual-role strokes, uncertain placement, and explicitly says the pass supplies no text/graphic code rule. The newly viewed f99v original additionally contains a prominent physical hole interrupting roughly three upper text lines; this latter observation is not independently re-extracted here.
design.distinct_scope: This is not pen-space, reflow, drawing-reset, correction chronology, or shared-stroke inference: the independent variable is an exogenous material hole, and the semantic decision is record continuity versus a hole-specific reset.
design.smallest_test: Using only the already admitted f99v source packet, transcribe the two line fragments bordering the hole and compare their record-level construction to one intact neighboring record, with reset criteria frozen before inspection. Do not infer missing text or treat the hole as a gap token.
design.reopen_condition: Reopen only if the existing source packet contains enough post-hole text to test both continuity and reset predictions; otherwise retain as an untestable raw hypothesis.
design.selection_status: raw unreviewed; no readiness, novelty, or positive evidence claim
